sentences.text: Hassiacosuchus was an extinct genus of small alligatorid.
The genus was named in 1935 by K. Weitzel, with the type species designated as H. haupti — the species the genus is based on.
A second species, H. kayi, was named in 1941 by C.C. Mook. The parent group of Hassiacosuchus is Globidonta, and it is classified in the class Reptilia.
Fossils of this animal have been found in Germany from the early Eocene, specifically at the famous Messel pit. It lived between 56 and 41.03 million years ago during the Ypresian to Lutetian stages.
Wassersug and Hecht argued in 1967 that Hassiacosuchus is synonymous with Allognathosuchus, though phylogenetic analyses later excluded H. haupti from that genus.
